topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text: Kid walks into my office, eyes a little wild, hands trembling—pretty sure he's got the weight of the world pinning him down. Says he's been accused of plagiarism. I’ve heard it before, but something in his voice, a flicker of desperation, tells me this one's different. I lean back, give him a slow nod, and let him talk. Been around the block enough to know when someone’s story’s straight, and this kid, he’s got a tale that’s worth untangling. I take the papers he slides across the desk, a wad of research and whatnot. Toss them aside. “First thing,” I say, “we find the truth.” He looks at me, a glimmer of hope flickering there. I know the drill, and I know this city. No stone's gonna be left unturned. This case, it’s starting to feel like old times.
